title: Taiwanese public grants run one year at a time and depend on the budget vote; this backs a dated range with a re-quote rule and gives an honest 'ten years pre-funded' contrast
problem: The MOC grant is single-year by default; multi-year (at most 2 years) is open only after 3 years in a row of funding; amounts depend on the Legislative Yuan budget and may be cut or stopped; each year's window is one month, announced separately; applicants must report operating status and site-use rights. So a Taiwanese public funder fixes numbers in yearly NT$ budgets, and a new residency would first apply once it exists. Two uses: (1) Laura's 2031 range is a pre-application signal; the firm figure enters a later budget, which supports CLIENT-12's 'quote date' and UNIQ-05's 're-quote rule'. (2) Laura's ten pre-funded years (2033-2042) are something this funder's own rules cannot offer. This is a sourced replacement for the misread Kresge 'sustain' note (L04-V1). It is an inference from one programme, not a general law.

title: Currency: Taiwan's residency grant rules are in NT$, so CLIENT-10's labelled FX line matters more for the fundraising excerpt
problem: CLIENT-10 was lowered to 'low' because the case never says the co-sponsors are Taiwanese or count in NT$. That is still true. But the one Taiwanese residency funder found writes every amount in NT$ (stipend, per-application cap, annual cap). If any co-sponsor is a Taiwanese public body, Laura's US$ range will be read in NT$. At 10-year USD/TWD volatility of 4.69% a year, a two-year 1-standard-deviation move is about 6.6% (MODEL, from VERIFIED FRED data to 18 Sep 2026). title: Taiwan's public-grant rules make a founder's figure a declared budget line that must match across funders; the range and later numbers must reconcile
problem: Under the Executive Yuan's rules for all central-government grants to private groups, a project that asks two or more public funders must list the whole budget and each funder's amount; hiding or faking cancels the grant and claws back money. Leftover money is returned in proportion to each funder's share. The MOC grant adds that a changed or failed plan must be reported for approval, and that rule breaches can bring recovery and a two-year bar. So in Taiwan's public setting, Laura's own contribution would be a declared number seen side by side with other funders' numbers. This supports the case's warning on overpromising (case:114-116) with a Taiwan-specific mechanism. Limit: penalties are for hiding or faking, not for an honest shortfall; the 2016 text is the version read.

title: Ladder-cost conflict ($294k vs $298.6k) explained; it changes today's floor estimate, not the 2031 co-sponsor logic
problem: The 16 Oct number sheet's $294,453 (headroom $5,547) prices $50,000 at each payment date (1 Jan 2033-2042) on a bootstrapped 15 Oct curve, carried forward to 1 Jan 2027. That is the value of the payments, i.e. an ideal zero-coupon match that is not buyable since the 6 Oct WInS-only email. The lenses' $298,624 (headroom $1,376, 4.7bp) prices to the WInS holdings' own earlier maturity dates (15 Dec for iBonds; Feb/May/Nov for the bonds) and assumes yields stay unchanged to 1 Jan 2027. On WInS dates with forward rates it is $297,778 (7.7bp). So about $3.3k of the gap is maturity dates and about $0.8k is 'unchanged' vs forward. The sheet says the 2028 deposit tops up any ladder gap first, which lowers the floor, so the $145k quoted floor is softer than shown. For co-sponsors this matters little: by 2031 the floor is already bought (Jan 2028) and is a known figure.
